beats.say: Which stock swung hardest in one day this week? Five tech and power names, lined up.

visual.big: Which stock swung hardest this week?

beats.say: Number five. Cerebras jumped eleven percent Friday after record revenue and a higher full-year forecast. Sales grew fifty-five percent, though it still lost money.
Number four. AMD rose thirteen percent Monday on an analyst upgrade and a Google cloud chip pick. Broadcom gained nearly nine percent too.

visual.reason: Analyst upgrade, Google Cloud chip pick

beats.say: Number three. Nebius fell seventeen percent Thursday after pushing back its seven billion dollar revenue run-rate goal to February. Its revenue still rose more than five hundred percent.
Number two. CoreWeave jumped twenty-five percent Wednesday after raising its revenue forecast. Sales beat its own outlook, and rival Nebius rose fifteen percent too.
And number one. Fervo Energy, a geothermal power company, surged twenty-six percent Monday after quarterly results showed about twelve billion dollars in power orders, including a Google deal.
Smaller, younger companies tend to swing more. Follow for one market move explained every day.
